title: El Ojo de Agua, VISTA STORIES
comment: ojo-cienegas (VISTA): lindero de una hacienda nogalera en Cuatro Ciénegas, Coahuila, junto a una cerca de alambre y postes viejos, a media tarde. Caras comunes, no famosas; los tres se distinguen a simple vista.

chars.TRANSITO_ELIZONDO: Mexican woman, the most feared landowner of the region, 58 years old, sun-tanned skin, short silver-streaked black hair swept back, sharp dark eyes, thin hard mouth, a black felt cowboy hat, a tan suede ranch jacket over a black blouse, dark jeans, tall brown boots, her hands empty.
chars.ANDRES_VILLARREAL: Mexican man, city lawyer and heir of the neighboring hacienda, 35 years old, fair skin, short neat brown hair, light stubble, rimless glasses, a navy blazer over a white shirt without tie, grey trousers, brown leather shoes, his hands empty.
chars.ROSENDO_AYALA: Mexican man, the landowner's loyal foreman, 54 years old, dark weathered skin, grey stubble, a straw cowboy hat, a red bandana around his neck, a faded beige work shirt, jeans, work boots, his hands empty.

locs.LOC_LINDEROCIENEGAS: Boundary line of a pecan hacienda in Cuatro Cienegas, Coahuila, in the dry mid-afternoon: an old barbed wire fence with crooked wooden posts, tall pecan trees on one side, desert scrub and pale mountains on the other, a dusty dirt road, a glimpse of a clear turquoise spring pool in the distance, a wooden table under a pecan tree, no readable text, no signs, no logos, no people.
